sections.content:
43,275 people

were counted on the census as "communication operators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Communication operators operate telecoms equipment to transmit and receive signals and messages.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "communication operators", 17.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "communication operators" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "communication operators" included:

  • pensions and insurance clerks and assistants
  • nannies and au pairs
  • human resources administrative occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "communication operators" there were more women than men (62.5% compared with 37.5%).

This means "communication operators" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "customer service occupations".

Men made up 37.5% and women made up 62.5% of "communication operators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "communication operators" included:

  • biochemists and biomedical scientists
  • advertising and marketing associate professionals
  • interior designers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "communication operators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "communication operators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "communication operators", 13.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.6% compared with 24.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.9%) than self-employed (3.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
